earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only wordlists/comparative notes (Nordenskiold 1905; Rivet 1910; Crequi-Montfort & Rivet 1913; Fleck 2013 overview); no grammar or phonology of Atsahuaca exists.

sources.citation: Créqui-Montfort, G. de & Paul Rivet. 1913. Linguistique bolivienne: Le groupe Otuké. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 10(1): 317-337 (transcription key p. 318 n. 2).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The Pano paper refers all transcription conventions to this note; it would say what the acute/breve accents on the Atsahuaka forms denote (tonic accent vs. length), which is needed before anyone infers a stress pattern from the wordlist.

sources.citation: Loos, Eugene E. 1999. 'Pano'. In R. M. W. Dixon & Alexandra Y. Aikhenvald (eds.), The Amazonian Languages (Cambridge Language Surveys), 227-250. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Listed only in Table 8.1 'Languages of the Pano family' as '12 [dagger] Atsawaca P' in 'The Chacobo subgroup'; no data. The chapter's prosody remarks (pp. 230-233: 'Some Pano languages have been reported to have distinctive tones.. in the cases that have been closely analysed, tone is predictable from the underlying syllable structure' [Capanawa]; 'Stress assignment often depends on the syllable structure of the word, but details vary from language to language. In Capanawa, Shipibo, Canamari and some others of the Capanawa subgroup, a closed second syllable is stressed') name other languages,…

sources.citation: Valenzuela, Pilar M. & Roberto Zariquiey. 2023. Language classification in Western Amazonia: Advances in favor of the Pano-Takana hypothesis. LIAMES 23: e023002, 1-53. doi 10.20396/liames.v23i00.8670150
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Atsawaka data or phonology; PDF read in the work dir and deleted (not kept).

sources.citation: Oliveira, Sanderson Castro Soares de. 2014. Contribuições para a reconstrução do Protopáno. Tese de doutorado, Universidade de Brasília. 492 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Per-language phonology summaries (with 'acento' paragraphs) exist only for the 19 languages retained; none for Atsawáka. The acute accents on the glottonyms (Atsawáka, Yamiáka) follow a naming convention ('representamos graficamente acento, segundo a pronúncia comum dessas palavras', p. 39), not a claim about the language.

sources.citation: Fleck, David W. 2013. Panoan languages and linguistics. Anthropological Papers of the AMNH 99. New York: AMNH.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Atsawaka stress. Lists the entire documentation of †Atsawaka as 'Nordenskiöld (1905: 275-276/1906: 526-527) 49-word list; Créqui-Montfort and Rivet (1913: 46-78) 223-word lexicon collected by Nordenskiöld' (pp. 96-97); Atsawaka/Yamiaka treated as two dialects of one language (p. 12, table 1).

sources.citation: Zariquiey Biondi, Roberto. 2011. A grammar of Kashibo-Kakataibo. PhD thesis, Research Centre for Linguistic Typology, La Trobe University.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Classification listing only; the grammar's prosody chapter is about Kashibo-Kakataibo.

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain. 2005-. Diccionario etnolingüístico y guía bibliográfica de los pueblos indígenas sudamericanos: Pano-Takana.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; Atsawaka appears only in the classification lists (†Atsawaca, Chacobo/southwestern subgroups).

sources.citation: Shell, Olive A. 1975 [3a ed. 2008]. Estudios panos III: Las lenguas pano y su reconstrucción. Serie Lingüística Peruana 12. Yarinacocha/Lima: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano. 212 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Atsahuaca forms appear only as comparanda in the cognate sets (ch. 6). On the old sources Shell says only 'en lo que respecta a los materiales antiguos, se ha respetado la forma como fueron registrados' (p. 14). The accent/tone discussion (acento de copla, acento fuerte vs débil, tono) concerns Shipibo-Conibo, Cashibo, Chácobo and Cashinahua, never At.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; entry reads 'Atsahuaca or Chaspa - spoken on the Carama River in the same country. [E. Nordenskiöld 1905, pp. 275-276.]' plus a short comparative wordlist.

sources.citation: Tovar, Antonio. 1961. Catálogo de las lenguas de America del Sur: enumeración, con indicaciones tipológicas, bibliografía y mapas. Buenos Aires: Editorial Sudamericana.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists 'Arasaire (o Arasa..), Atsahuaca o Caspa (con el subgrupo de los Yamiaca o Haauñeiri, junto al río Yaguarmayo) y los Arauá' as a Pano group; classification only, nothing typological.

sources.citation: Mason, J. Alden. 1950. 'The languages of South American Indians'. In Julian H. Steward (ed.), Handbook of South American Indians, vol. 6 (Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 143), 157-317. Washington: Smithsonian Institution.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'The Atsawaca (Atsahuaka, etc.) or Chaspa, and the Yamiaca (Yamiaka) or Hasuneiri dialects (?) must be very similar, as they are said to have separated in historic times.. Some of the Arasa and Atsawaca also speak Tacana'; classification only, no phonology.

sources.citation: Steward, Julian H. & Alfred Métraux. 1948. 'Tribes of the Peruvian and Ecuadorian Montaña'. In J. H. Steward (ed.), Handbook of South American Indians, vol. 3: The Tropical Forest Tribes (BAE Bulletin 143), 535-656. Washington: Smithsonian Institution.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnographic only ('The Atsahuaca, of whom only 20 survived in 1904, lived along the Carama (Atsahuaca) and the.. The Yamiaca, who live on the Yaguarmayo River.. are a branch of the Atsahuaca'); nothing linguistic beyond affiliation.

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul & Constant Tastevin. 1927. Les dialectes Pano du haut Juruá et du haut Purús. Anthropos 22: 811-827 (first instalment; continued in later volumes).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on accent or stress in pp. 811-827 (a full-text search for stress/accent/tonique/syllabe empty); the only transcription note explains two consonant letters ('un son intermédiaire entre cy et ty'; 'entre l et r'). The 'accent-second sur dernière syllabe' passages that archive.org's full-text search co-locates in this volume belong to A. Mostaert's article on Ordos Mongol (pp. 182-183), not to this paper.

sources.citation: Créqui-Montfort, Georges de & Paul Rivet. 1921-1922. La famille linguistique Takana. Journal de la Société des Américanistes n.s. 13(1): 91-102; 13(2): 281-301; 14-15: 121-167 and 141-182. doi 10.3406/jsa.1921.2906, 10.3406/jsa.1921.2923, 10.3406/jsa.1922.3996, 10.3406/jsa.1922.3913
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. All four parts were searched for accent/tonique/transcri/prononc/orthograph/graphie/syllabe with no hit; the Atsahuaka material is cited lexically and for pronouns only, with Nordenskiöld's accent marks reproduced but never commented on.

sources.citation: Créqui-Montfort, G. de & Paul Rivet. 1913. Linguistique bolivienne: Les dialectes Pano de Bolivie. Le Muséon n.s. 14: 19-78.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress/accent. Pages 24-41 give notes on genre, nombre, pronoms, suffixes; pp. 41-45 give 'correspondances de voyelles et de consonnes' only; pp. 46-78 the comparative vocabulary in which Atsahuaka ('At', Nordenskiöld's 223-word list) forms carry accent marks (kǎkámǎ 'ananas', héuvi 'arbre', šinosǒko 'grande araignée') whose meaning is referred to a note in their Otuké paper (JSA 10, p. 318 n. 2). No accent rule.

sources.citation: Marcou, Philippe. 1913. [Compte rendu:] Créqui-Montfort (G. de) et Rivet (P.), Linguistique bolivienne. Les dialectes Pano de Bolivie. Journal de la Société des Américanistes n.s. 10(2): 655-656.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonetic content; comments concern possessive adjectives and imperative suffixes and a few Pano-Nahuatl lookalikes.

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul. 1910. Sur quelques dialectes panos peu connus. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 7: 221-242.
sources.access_detail: read online, no copy kept
sources.note: The only other primary publication of Nordenskiöld's Atsahuaca/Yamiaca material; would confirm whether Rivet added any remark on accent marks. Per Créqui-Montfort & Rivet 1913 it only reproduces the vocabularies, so low expected yield.

sources.citation: Nordenskiöld, Erland. 1906. Resa i Perus och Bolivias gränstrakter, företagen med understöd af Vega- och Wahlbergsstipendierna. Redogörelse för de etnografiska och arkeologiska arbetena. Ymer 26(1): 60-84.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology content: states only that Atsahuaca and Yamiaca are 'pano-talande', that Yamiaca mix in many Tacana words, and that the Atsahuaca gave numerals 1-5 (pp. 77-78); refers to the 1905 Ymer article for the language data.

sources.citation: Nordenskiöld, Erland. 1905. Beiträge zur Kenntnis einiger Indianerstämme des Rio Madre de Dios-Gebietes. Ymer 25: 265-312 (Atsahuaca wordlist pp. 275-276).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress statement. Only a pronunciation key before the 49-word Atsahuaca column: 'Die Aussprache im allgemeinen wie Spanisch' (p. 275) with s-hacek, ä, w, ö, l explained; forms carry acute accents (páucani 'Ohr', macáni 'Hand', récani 'Nase', hána 'Zunge', umapása 'Wasser', chinapóto 'Asche', huári 'Sonne', óse 'Mond', usáqui 'schlafen', mastára 'schlecht') but their meaning is never stated and no rule is given.

sources.citation: Nordenskiöld, Erland. 1905. Exploration scientifique au Pérou et en Bolivie (1904-1905). La Géographie: Bulletin de la Société de géographie 12(5) (15 novembre 1905): 289-[297].
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No linguistic data beyond the classificatory sentence; the rest is ethnography, archaeology, geology and collections. No wordlist, no pronunciation remarks.

sources.citation: Lyon, Patricia J. 1975. Dislocación tribal y clasificaciones lingüísticas en la zona del río Madre de Dios. Actas del XXXIX Congreso Internacional de Americanistas 5: 185-207. Lima: IEP.
